subtitle: std::<version> — the C++20 header that aggregates every __cpp_lib_* library feature-test macro and nothing else (no types, functions, or objects). re_std surfaces those macros by including the platform <version> when the language is C++20 or later: the __cpp_lib_* macros describe std's library and cannot be reimplemented, so they are re-exported unchanged (identity preserved). Before C++20 there is no aggregator — the per-feature __cpp_lib_* macros (added to individual headers in C++17) have no umbrella — and re_std's own capability signalling is its D_RE_STD_* / D_ENV_* detection table (see <djinterp>), not __cpp_lib_*; re_std's <version> is intentionally a no-op there. Because the header is macro-only, it has a single catalogued row standing for the whole __cpp_lib_* set rather than per-symbol coverage. No unmet re_std dependencies.
legend_blurb: Coverage of the C++20 <version> header — a macro-only feature-test aggregator. re_std re-exports std's __cpp_lib_* macros by including <version> on C++20+ (identity preserved; they describe std and cannot be reimplemented). No pre-C++20 aggregator exists; re_std's own capability macros are the D_RE_STD_*/D_ENV_* table, not __cpp_lib_*.

symbols.name: __cpp_lib_* feature-test macros
symbols.notes: The entire __cpp_lib_* macro set, surfaced as an identity-preserving re-export: re_std's <version> includes the platform <version> on C++20+ (gated on D_ENV_LANG_IS_CPP20_OR_HIGHER, guarded by __has_include). These macros describe std's library, so re_std cannot define or reimplement them — it surfaces std's unchanged. constexpr is not applicable (preprocessor macros). One row stands for the whole set since the header is macro-only. Pre-C++20, re_std exposes its own D_RE_STD_*/D_ENV_* detection table instead (documented in <djinterp>), which is re_std-authored and tracked separately, not here.
symbols.failure_reason: Cannot reach below C++20. <version> is the C++20 aggregator of the __cpp_lib_* macros; before C++20 those macros live in their individual feature headers (C++17) with no umbrella header to surface, and re_std will not fabricate __cpp_lib_* values (they describe std's library, not re_std's). re_std's pre-C++20 capability signalling uses its own D_RE_STD_*/D_ENV_* macros.
